methodological_rigor.justification: The study analyzes 82 high-risk NMIBC tumors treated with BCG using imaging mass cytometry, with predefined endpoints (BCG response/failure, RFS, PFS) and appropriate retrospective clinical annotation. It applies single-cell clustering and compartment-normalized indices with nonparametric testing and FDR correction, and uses Cox models for time-to-event associations, which is reasonable for exploratory biomarker work. However, the ML component is underpowered (69 patients for modeling, split into 59 train and 10 independent test), and the strong headline accuracy (9/10) rests on a very small hold-out cohort with acknowledged instability and no external validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The clinical problem is high impact: identifying BCG nonresponders early in high-risk NMIBC could meaningfully change management. The manuscript evaluates real BCG-treated patient material with recurrence/progression outcomes, but the evidence is retrospective and biomarker-discovery oriented rather than a prospective validation or intervention study. This supports an Oxford LoE of 4 (retrospective prognostic/predictive biomarker associations with exploratory model development).

reporting_quality.justification: No single checklist (CONSORT/STROBE/TRIPOD) fully captures the combined spatial single-cell profiling plus image-bag MIL pipeline, so 'other' is the most accurate designation. The manuscript reports cohort selection from an initial 427-sample TMA set down to 82 analyzable IMC samples, defines BCG response/failure criteria, and specifies the statistical workflow (indices, tests, FDR correction, Cox models) and ML evaluation approach, including patient-level train/test splitting. Reproducibility is limited by the blinded text: public deposition of IMC raw data, trained models, and code is not described, and the GA-MIL validation is constrained to a 10-patient hold-out set.

novelty_literature.justification: The combination of spatial single-cell IMC profiling with an IMC-specific gated attention multiple instance learning classifier for BCG response prediction is a substantial methodological extension beyond bulk subtyping. The work highlights spatially defined protective versus high-risk features (e.g., immune cells localized within tumor regions versus fibroblast/plasma-cell enrichment) and connects them to outcomes. Novelty is reduced by the exploratory nature and limited external validation, but the approach is meaningfully more advanced than standard clinicopathologic predictors.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized, with clear definitions of responder/nonresponder endpoints, transparent sample attrition, and a detailed description of the IMC processing and statistical indices. The discussion is appropriately cautious, repeatedly labeling findings as exploratory and noting the small independent test set for the ML model. Some sections are necessarily technical, but the main claims and limitations remain readable and interpretable.

key_strengths: Directly addresses an important unmet need in high-risk NMIBC: predicting BCG failure using tumor microenvironment features.
Leverages spatial single-cell IMC on 82 BCG-treated tumors with defined clinical endpoints (RFS/PFS) and incorporates multiple-comparison control via FDR.
Reports interpretable biological signals (e.g., fibroblast enrichment in nonresponders; plasma-cell signals associated with progression; immune cells within tumor compartment protective).
Implements a patient-level split and an independent hold-out cohort for the IMC-GA-MIL model, reducing leakage risk relative to patch-level splitting.
key_concerns: The ML validation is extremely small (10-patient hold-out set), so performance estimates (e.g., 9/10 accuracy) are unstable and could regress substantially in external cohorts.
Retrospective multi-center sampling and substantial missingness in some clinical variables (e.g., tumor size unreported in many cases) may introduce unmeasured confounding.
No external IMC cohort with a matched marker panel is available in this study, limiting generalizability and transportability of the classifier.
Data/code availability is unclear from the blinded manuscript, limiting reproducibility of both the single-cell pipeline and the GA-MIL model.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a strong exploratory translational study with sophisticated spatial profiling and a plausible mechanistic link to BCG resistance, but the classifier component needs substantially stronger validation. With external replication and clearer reproducibility commitments, the work could plausibly land in a tier 2 venue; at present it fits tier 2 only with major revisions.
